newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's central bank sells dollars at 892.40.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's central bank sells dollars at 892.40.

text.p: South Korea's central bank sold dollars at 892.40 in Wednesday morning trading to limit the won's fall following a decision by local banks on Tuesday to bail out the Kia Group, dealers said.
The dollar fell to 891.60 just after the Bank of Korea's intervention.

"We felt a need to suppress the dollar buying sentiment in the market to prevent the won from falling," said a government official in charge of foreign exchange. "Dollar supply has been growing tight as dealers are covering their short positions, the dollar is strengthening against the yen and banks decided to bail out Kia Group," he said.
The won opened at 892.20 on Wednesday against its Tuesday closing level of 891.90.
